validity.population: healthy adult cohort from Wong et al. 2014 mapped to the schematic BVS95 graph
validity.physiological_state: supine bicycle exercise; global-flow sensitivity profile
validity.description: Cardiac output is multiplied by the 1.9-fold cohort result. Regional redistribution is intentionally not applied because the BVS95 branches are not a validated upper/lower-body territorial partition.

sources.citation: Wong DT et al. Changes in systemic and pulmonary blood flow distribution in normal adult volunteers in response to posture and exercise. J Physiol Sci. 2014;64:105-112. doi:10.1007/s12576-013-0298-z.
sources.license: Citation and derived multiplier only; article rights remain with the publisher.

limitations: This is a global-flow sensitivity scenario, not a complete physiological exercise model.
The source reports 1.5-fold upper-body and 2.3-fold lower-body flow increases, but BVS95 lacks a validated mapping for applying those regional factors without inventing anatomy.
The cohort value is not sex-specific and does not define exercise power for an individual.
Fixed schematic cross-sections turn increased flow into proportionally increased mean velocity.
